findings.finding: The shown required/full benchmark paths use frozen semantic scores, so they do not directly score the newly generated embeddings. Seal is called without reports and records trusted-pipeline provenance with passed flags. Frozen-HEAD main wiring read after the reviews confirms requiredFeatures is passed for full coverage too. This is a gap in what the gate attests, not proof that a damaged bundle reached production. embeddingsStale validates model/profile/key/dimension contracts; arbitrary model-revision changes may be rejected elsewhere, so the clean counterexample is changed semantic values that still satisfy those contracts.

findings.disposition: supported representativeness question; reject production-zero inference
findings.finding: The nested immutable-baseline run still enforces exact candidate features; current source data is then measured with the frozen semantic observations and quality floors. That is not wholesale removal of the integrity check. A new or renamed venue may have no frozen semantic score in this gate, so a semantically competitive new venue is a useful negative-control proposal. It does not follow that production always gives that venue zero semantic score or excludes it from top-5. The supplied test adds an unrelated venue and checks feature tampering, not the proposed semantic competition.

findings.disposition: supported provenance gap with bounded implications
findings.finding: The baseline file is versioned but is not an input to benchmark_content_id, and the shown bundle reuse condition checks semantic_content_id and passed strings, not current gate/fixture identity. The exact frozen semantic-content implementation confirms that it hashes semantic inputs, not the benchmark gate. A gate-only change can therefore reuse a previously sealed bundle without running that workflow's new gates. Separate CI still runs its required checks; branch protection and actual workflow histories were not inspected. Jointly changing versioned fixtures is not by itself evidence of malicious tampering or inevitable degradation.

findings.disposition: supported conditional liveness counterexample; occurrence unverified
findings.finding: Default GitHub concurrency can replace an already pending run even when cancel-in-progress is false. A late stale workflow_run can therefore displace a newer pending push and then be skipped, leaving publication delayed if no subsequent successful bundle/event recovers it. This is a liveness possibility, not a observed outage or proof that main publication is always monotonic. Absence of a past canceled run would not refute the structural counterexample. Retain exact-current-SHA checks while considering queue policy.

findings.disposition: supported failure-to-skip path with corrected shell rationale
findings.finding: The early git ls-remote | cut pipeline can mask git failure because default bash has -e but not pipefail. An empty current_main is then reported as a stale trigger and skips publication. The later equality test fails on an empty SHA, so this is a missed-publication/diagnostic issue, not evidence of stale deployment. Agy's proposal to accept an ancestor instead of exact current main weakens the existing policy and is not adopted.
